name: tensorviz-vscode
description: Explore PyTorch and JAX/Flax model graphs, inspect tensor shapes, jump to Python source, and review PyTorch architecture changes in VS Code.
//icon: Marketplace / Extensions-view logo. A committed 512x512 PNG of the website brand mark (icons/icon.png). VS Code requires a raster icon here (SVG is not allowed for the top-level icon field) and at least 128x128.
//extensionKind: Runs with workspace files, backend and trace worker on local desktop or Remote SSH. Other remote kinds are unsupported.
//activationEvents: Activate the views and index already-open Python documents. In a trusted workspace, a Python subclass can start source discovery; only discovered models receive CodeLenses. Static indexing does not execute the model.
//enabledApiProposals: Keep proposed APIs absent for released VS Code compatibility. Optional fork APIs are granted by its product configuration and probed at runtime.

contributes.//viewsContainers: A committed SVG under extension/icons/ (extension/media/ is gitignored — it is where the built React app is staged — so an icon there would never be committed). icons/tensorviz.svg is the website brand mark drawn with stroke=currentColor and a transparent background so VS Code can tint it to the active/inactive activity-bar color.
contributes.//configurationDefaults: Only tensorviz settings belong here; preserve the user's editor, language and theme preferences.

tensorviz.agent.codexPath.markdownDescription: Optional absolute path to the Codex executable for Canvas chat. Empty uses the workspace host's PATH and standard installation locations. Sign in to the installed agent first. In Remote SSH, this path and sign-in belong to the SSH server.

tensorviz.agent.claudePath.markdownDescription: Optional absolute path to the Claude Code executable for Canvas chat. Empty uses the workspace host's PATH and standard installation locations. Sign in to the installed agent first. In Remote SSH, this path and sign-in belong to the SSH server.

tensorviz.mcpPort.description: Local MCP port shared by all tensorViz windows. Zero automatically chooses an available port and reuses it while available. Set a number to require a fixed port. Applies when connecting from the status bar. Copy the current URL from tensorViz when configuring an agent.

tensorviz.repoPath.markdownDescription: **Developer override.** Absolute path to a canvas checkout, used as the backend source instead of the one tensorViz ships with. You do not need this: the backend is bundled with the app and packaged inside the extension, and is found first. It exists for running against a checkout. When set, it is used as-is — tensorViz will not fall back to guessing if it does not validate.

tensorviz.pythonPath.markdownDescription: Absolute Python path offered in the environment picker and used for model execution when this workspace folder has no saved choice. Use tensorViz: Select Python Environment to choose a Conda/venv for the model’s owning folder. The tensorViz service has its own Python. Missing capture/model libraries require approval and existing Torch/CUDA versions are preserved.

tensorviz.devServerUrl.markdownDescription: Load the canvas from this URL instead of the app bundled with the extension — for developing the frontend against a live `npm start`. When empty (the default) the backend serves the built app on a port chosen at launch. The value is used verbatim, and its origin becomes the panel's `frame-src`.

enumDescriptions: Legacy value; opens the sidebar Canvas. Use Open Canvas in Browser explicitly.
Legacy value; opens the sidebar Canvas.
tensorviz.graphSurface.markdownDescription: Open as Graph always uses the persistent sidebar Canvas. Use **tensorViz: Open Canvas in Browser** for the selected model or project.
tensorviz.graphSurface.deprecationMessage: All values now open the sidebar Canvas. Remove this setting; use tensorViz: Open Canvas in Browser for external opening.

tensorviz.autoOpenCanvas.markdownDescription: Open the sidebar Canvas initially when a Python model or project is found. Only tensorViz IDE enables this implicitly; stock VS Code requires an explicit setting or Open as Graph. Opening another editor never replaces the selected model/project. The existing toggle shortcut shows or hides the retained Canvas.

tensorviz.traceOnSave.markdownDescription: Validate the selected model after saving changed model code or a known Python dependency. Rapid saves are combined; validation uses the saved inputs, device and environment. Source-only inspection and an editor auto-open that has not run stay source-only. Disable to refresh source without running.

tensorviz.showGraphPrompt.markdownDescription: Show an Open as Graph notification when the active saved Python file contains a discovered PyTorch model. Each file is offered once per VS Code window session. Disable this to keep using CodeLens, Models or the command palette without notifications.

enumDescriptions: Real tensors, except models already seen with at least 150M parameters (about 600 MB in float32), which use fake tensors.
tensorviz.traceTier.markdownDescription: How the trace worker runs your model when it captures a graph without a saved profile. `real` (default) uses real tensors, so data-dependent control flow (`if x.sum() > 0`) takes a branch. `fake` (experimental) builds the model, its inputs and the forward under `FakeTensorMode`: no weights are allocated and the same graph is drawn, with shapes but no tensor values. A model that needs values (`.item()`, `nonzero`, `unique`, a lazy module) is re-run once with real tensors. `auto` (experimental) runs a model with real tensors the first time, and with fake tensors from then on if that run counted at least 150M parameters (below that, fake tensors measured slower); a large model that needed the real re-run stays real. Fake tensors are faster for large models and slower (about 0.6 s) for small ones. Saved profiles, validation and candidates always use real tensors.

enumDescriptions: No execution cache. Every Run executes your model exactly as before.

Diagnostic only: every Run still executes your model. tensorViz also keeps the result in memory and, when a later Run has exactly the same inputs, compares the two and writes the outcome to the tensorViz output channel. A stored result is never shown.

Default: when a Run has exactly the same inputs as an earlier Run in this window, tensorViz shows that earlier result instead of running your model again, labelled "Reused identical result … (model not run again)". Use Run fresh to execute anyway.
tensorviz.executionCache.mode.markdownDescription: Reuse of identical runs (on by default; set `off` to always run). A Run can reuse an earlier identical result only with the same saved sources, configuration, inputs and seed, environment variables, Python environment and tensorViz backend, on CPU, with nothing read, listed or checked for outside the tracked files and no native code loaded beyond Python's, torch's and numpy's own. `shadow` only checks this, without changing what you see; `on` shows the earlier result instead of running your model again (Python still runs briefly to check that nothing changed). Agent (MCP) runs always run. Results are kept in memory for this window only and are never written to disk; **tensorViz: Clear Execution Cache** drops them. Takes effect on the next Run.

tensorviz.executionCache.maxSizeMB.markdownDescription: Memory limit, in megabytes, for results kept by `#tensorviz.executionCache.mode#` in this window (at most 32 results, 16 MB each). The least recently used result is dropped first.

tensorviz.followEditor.description: Move the project canvas to the file you open, and open its node. Turn this off to leave the camera where you put it; the canvas still follows when you click a node yourself.

tensorviz.codeFocus.markdownDescription: Dim code outside selected Canvas nodes. Configure **Model / class**, **Function**, or **Node / expression**, parameter declarations/uses, and opacity from **Code focus** in the Canvas toolbar. Preferences persist across sessions; hidden, stale, or unmapped views leave source undimmed.

tensorviz.agent.pipeline.markdownDescription: Canvas chat runtime. Native keeps the existing CLI bridge; ACP uses persistent Agent Client Protocol sessions. Set adapter paths and start a new chat after switching. ACP adapters are installed separately on the workspace host.

tensorviz.agent.codexAcpPath.markdownDescription: Absolute executable path for the optional ACP pipeline. Tested adapter: `@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp@2.3.0`. Uses the existing signed-in agent; no provider key goes to Canvas. Install explicitly; TensorViz never downloads or installs an adapter on Send.

tensorviz.agent.claudeAcpPath.markdownDescription: Absolute executable path for the optional ACP pipeline. Tested adapter: `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp@0.99.0`. Uses the existing signed-in agent; no provider key goes to Canvas. Install explicitly; TensorViz never downloads or installs an adapter on Send.

scripts.//pretest: Clean out/ before tests because tsc does not remove outputs for deleted source files. Compile and watch remain incremental.
scripts.pretest: npm run clean && npm run compile
scripts.//test:unit:interpreter: Compatibility alias for test:integration. Python workers and MCP evidence tests require TENSORVIZ_TEST_PYTHON, or the repository venv.
scripts.test: npm run test:unit && npm run test:unit:interpreter && npm run test:electron
scripts.package: npm run stage:backend && vsce package --no-dependencies && node scripts/verify-package.mjs
scripts.package:release: node scripts/verify-package.mjs --require-release-key && npm run stage:backend && vsce package --no-dependencies && node scripts/verify-package.mjs --release
scripts.//vsix: Build a local VSIX in order: ensure dependencies, build:webview, compile, package. package uses the existing webview build; keeping the steps separate avoids duplicate builds in release-vsix.yml. See docs/releasing.md.
scripts.//dev:build: Build the webpage before staging the backend and compiled host for F5, then check that all three outputs are current.
scripts.dev:build: npm run build:webview && npm run stage:backend && npm run compile && npm run check:staged
